message.content:
**PAGE: Image 1 — Admin Dashboard**
- **ISSUE 1:** [SEVERITY: moderate] **Top stat row (6 cards)** – The six metric cards (NGOs, Volunteers, Campaigns, Staff, Open Reports, Suspended) appear to have *slightly* unequal widths or internal padding. The label/value pairs don’t feel perfectly locked to a shared vertical rhythm; the gap between the icon and the label varies subtly between cards (e.g., “Suspended” feels tighter than “NGOs”). This breaks the grid’s visual beat.
- **ISSUE 2:** [SEVERITY: minor] **“NGOs awaiting approval” card** – The single list item inside this section has noticeably more vertical padding than the multi-item lists below (“Volunteers awaiting verification” has two items). The empty space below the single row looks like an orphaned whitespace block rather than intentional breathing room.
- **ISSUE 3:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Button group alignment** – In the “Volunteer reports” card, the three action buttons (Suspend, Mark reviewed, Dismiss) are right-aligned but their internal spacing (gap between buttons) appears slightly wider than the button groups in the cards above (Approve/Reject/Suspend). Inconsistent button-rhythm across sibling sections.
- **ISSUE 4:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Bottom stat row (3 cards)** – The “Platform stats” row at the very bottom uses only 3 cards vs. 6 in the top row. While logically different, the card height and internal padding differ from the top stat cards (the bottom ones are taller with more whitespace), creating a subtle size inconsistency for elements that share the same “stat card” component role.
- **ISSUE 5:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Section title typography** – The card headers (“NGOs awaiting approval”, “Volunteer reports”, etc.) use a consistent weight, but the vertical spacing between the header and its description line is not uniform across all cards; some feel slightly looser than others.

---

**PAGE: Image 2 — NGO Dashboard (Green Earth Foundation)**
- **ISSUE 1:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Top stat cards (4 cards)** – The four metric cards (Campaigns, Applications, Funds Left, Rating) have good width consistency, but the “Funds Left” value (“₹50,000”) is visually heavier/taller due to the currency symbol, causing that card’s content area to sit slightly differently than its siblings. Minor baseline misalignment.
- **ISSUE 2:** [SEVERITY: moderate] **Campaign cards (bottom section)** – The two campaign cards (“River Clean-Up Drive”, “Tree Plantation Marathon”) have **unequal heights**. The left card’s content (badges + title + meta + progress bar) wraps or sits in a way that makes it visibly shorter than the right card. In a side-by-side grid, sibling cards must have equal height to maintain the card-stack rhythm.
- **ISSUE 3:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Badge/pill inconsistency** – The status badges inside the campaign cards use a pill shape with rounded-full radii, whereas the “UPCOMING” badge in the “Applications waiting for you” section above uses a slightly different background tint and possibly padding. The badge language should be identical across both list and card contexts.
- **ISSUE 4:** [SEVERITY: minor] **“View all” link position** – The “View all” text next to “Your campaigns” is floated to the far right with no accompanying icon or button treatment. It looks like plain text accidentally placed there rather than a deliberate navigation element, breaking the section-header pattern used elsewhere on the page.

---

**PAGE: Image 3 — Volunteer Dashboard (Priya Sharma)**
- **ISSUE 1:** [SEVERITY: moderate] **Two-column layout height mismatch** – The left column (“My campaigns”) and right column (“My applications”) are **not equal in height**. The left column extends further down because it contains three list items vs. the right column’s three items plus a funds card, but the container backgrounds do not align at the bottom. This creates a jagged, unbalanced visual edge between the two columns.
- **ISSUE 2:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Card internal spacing** – Inside “My campaigns” and “My applications”, the list items have consistent row height, but the padding between the last list item and the card’s bottom edge differs between the two cards. One feels more cramped at the base.
- **ISSUE 3:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Status badge color language** – The “ONGOING” badge (green tint), “COMPLETED” (gray), “ACCEPTED” (green), “UPCOMING” (blue), and “PENDING” (orange/beige) introduce many colors. While semantically distinct, the sheer variety of status colors across just this one page (5+ hues) reduces the system’s visual cohesion. Consider limiting to 3–4 semantic colors max.
- **ISSUE 4:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Empty state / minimal state** – The “My chat rooms” card shows one item (“Planning Room”) with no action button, while “Funds allocated to me” shows one item with a “PENDING” badge. The asymmetry of having an actionable status on one and plain text on the other (for single-item lists) feels slightly unfinished.

---

**PAGE: Image 4 — Browse Campaigns (Public Listing)**
- **ISSUE 1:** [SEVERITY: critical] **Card height inequality (major rhythm break)** – The three campaign cards in the main grid have **wildly different heights**. The middle card (“After-School Tutoring Program”) is significantly taller than the left and right cards because its content (title, org name, verified badge, stars, location, date range, funds) takes more vertical space or has more padding. In a 3-column grid, all cards **must** be equal height (using flex/grid stretch) so their bottom edges align perfectly. Currently, the staggered bottoms destroy the horizontal rhythm.
- **ISSUE 2:** [SEVERITY: moderate] **Progress bar inconsistency** – The funding progress bars at the bottom of each card are not aligned to a common baseline because the cards themselves are different heights. Additionally, the bar fill lengths appear to use different visual weights or the gray track thickness varies subtly between cards.
- **ISSUE 3:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Text truncation** – The organization names (“Green Earth Foun…”, “Bright Futures Tr…”) are truncated with ellipsis, which is correct, but the truncation point cuts off at different character widths, making the lines above the rating stars look ragged. Consider fixing the org name width or allowing wrapping with a max-line clamp instead.
- **ISSUE 4:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Search bar vs. dropdown alignment** – The search input field and the “All statuses” dropdown are side-by-side but their heights do not match exactly; the dropdown appears 1–2px shorter than the input, creating a slight misalignment in the control row.

---

**PAGE: Image 5 — Landing Page (Marketing/Home)**
- **ISSUE 1:** [SEVERITY: critical] **Massive vertical orphan whitespace** – Below the hero section (headline + CTA buttons + Field Overview card), there is an enormous expanse of empty dark green space (approximately 60–70% of the viewport height) with no content, no subtle pattern, no gradient fade, or footer anchor. It looks like the page failed to load lower sections or the layout is broken. This is a severe visual rhythm failure—the page simply “ends” visually too early.
- **ISSUE 2:** [SEVERITY: moderate] **Field Overview card positioning** – The “Field Overview” card floats to the right of the headline, but its vertical centering relative to the headline text feels slightly off (the card sits a bit low). The gap between the headline’s baseline and the card’s top edge is not harmoniously proportioned to the gap below the buttons.
- **ISSUE 3:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Button pair inconsistency** – The primary button (“Sign up as an NGO”) has a solid green background with an arrow icon, while the secondary button (“Sign up as a volunteer”) is a ghost/outline variant. Their internal padding looks similar, but the font weight or letter-spacing of the label text may differ slightly, making them feel like they come from different component families.
- **ISSUE 4:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Footer visibility** – The footer (“© 2026 Sanjivani…”) is pushed to the absolute bottom of the extremely long page, separated from the last meaningful content by ~1000px of void. If this is intended as a “full-height hero” design, the footer should either stick to the viewport bottom or the empty space should contain decorative elements (grid dots, faint map, etc.) to avoid looking like a rendering bug.
- **ISSUE 5:** [SEVERITY: minor] **Typography scale jump** – The headline (“Run every campaign…”) is very large (display size), but the body copy below it drops to a relatively small size without an intermediate subheading level. The contrast is stark and creates a jarring hierarchy leap.
